newsitem.title: GERMANY: BAYER SAYS JAN/FEB PROFIT WELL ABOVE PLAN.
newsitem.headline: BAYER SAYS JAN/FEB PROFIT WELL ABOVE PLAN.

text.p: German chemicals group Bayer AG said on Tuesday that profit in the first two months of 1997 was well above plan and that sales grew eight percent in the period.

"During the first two months we posted a sturdy sales increase of eight percent and the profits clearly exceeded our plans," Bayer chief executive Manfred Schneider told the company's annual news conference.

Bayer said it planned to raise its sales to 50 billion marks ($29.6 billion) in 1997 from 48.6 billion in 1996. It aimed at least to match profits achieved in 1996 when it made pre-tax profit of 4.46 billion marks.
Bayer said that it had a realistic chance to top its 1996 profits this year.
"We have a good chance that we will match the 1996 profit and a realistic chance that we will top it," Schneider said.
He said the group's planning is realistically cautious because of concerns about price levels.
Bayer had said that despite an expectation for stonger growth, increased international competition would make it difficult to significantly adjust prices.
